newsitem.title: UK: AT&T creates 250 UK jobs, beefs up network.
newsitem.headline: AT&T creates 250 UK jobs, beefs up network.

text.p: U.S. telephone giant AT & T Corp said on Monday it was creating 250 new jobs and a new global network centre to beef up its national network and meet growing demands from customers.
The company, which already employs 2,500 staff in Britain, said calling volume on its UK network had grown ten fold in the past 12 months and it was now carrying more than on million calls per day.

"The new positions are required to handle increasing demand from new and existing customers," the company said in a statement. "The new employees will perform a variety of tasks including customer care, network operations, sales and marketing."

Since it launched its full service in January 1996, AT&T has won 2,000 business customers and the company said it was providing communications services to 15 percent of the UK-based multinational companies -- the most valued customers of global telecoms companies.
AT&T's new network operations centre, in the heart of London, will support the company's UK network which in turn is linked to AT&T's world-wide intelligent network.

The building will also house the company's customer care centre providing 24-hour support to business and residential users throughout the country, housing 500 staff and supplementing existing locations, AT&T said.

"AT&T UK has seen 40 percent revenue growth in the last year," said Dennis Roth, the newly-appointed president and chief executive officer of AT&T UK. "We are investing in the UK to offer our customers a host of innovative and value-added services."
